item.title: Re: The rubbish station
item.content:encoded:
Hey! I am here from summon on SCPD Discord!

Crit
– hide block

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a full functional space station, made out of space debris and it builds more modules if it collects more space debris.

Love it! Nice and simple setting! Fantastic!

Central Narrative: The foundation decides to explore the SCP up close, revealing that there is a crew on board. The foundation attempts to contact them to ask questions.

This is pretty standard location anomaly stuff. Establish contact and determine properties. But there are many ways to add this in your article. What are you planning to do to make this an important part of the article? Or is this just setting up the rest?

The crew members don't exactly remember how they got there or anything about the station, only telling the things they DO remember.

What kinds of things DO they remember that will help the Foundation and the reader figure things out?

The foundation concludes by what the members have said that they are the creators of the space station who erased their own memories.

This is a weird thing for them to do and an especially weird thing to be able to figure out from interviews. Why do you think they erased their memories? What clues let the Foundation and the readers figure this out actively while moving through your world?

After the conclusion was made, they decide to try to figure out where the crew came from, where and how they built and launched the station without anyone noticing, etc.

How do they do that? What interesting details and hints are you going to go through? Is this DNA testing and more interviews or is it more like tracking movements and looking at missing persons? What are you planning to make this mysterious but also not confusing or vague?

By the end of the article, instead of knocking the scp out of orbit, the foundation decides to put the scp to use for research purposes.

Making SCiPs useful can be a bit of a trap. What exactly makes this anomaly useful for research above a station of their own design and knowledge? That's like finding a popsicle on the ground (but it looks clean) and you decide to eat that one instead of the one in your hand already. There needs to be some logic behind using the unknown object that they don't fully understand and wasn't designed specifically for them instead of something they control. Money isn't really an issue for the Foundation (unless you want it to be) so think about the rationale.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Getting to explore a few new characters in an unusual setting, slowly solving a mystery in the process

You've told me about your mystery (the origins and such) but not about your characters. If this is your hook, can you tell me more about them?

Additional Notes: I am completely lost at what I should do with the story, so feel free to make suggestions.

I have some Ideas I might propose to you but first I would love to see how you answer these questions. It is your story first and foremost :)

Can't wait to hear more!

item.title: Re: The rubbish station
item.content:encoded:
[Placeholder from PM]

My apologies for the delay in getting to you.

Given the length of time since my previous critique, I'm going to be treating this as effectively a new idea and not making comparisons to the previous version.

[+] Critique
[-] Critique

The core here is fairly solid. It presents a mystery that gives the plot some impetus, which is a stronger opening than many concepts get. My issue lies in that the extrapolation from this mystery is very plain and entirely unexciting. There's the mystery of who the crew are, the Foundation concludes they are the creators of the space station. There's a mystery of how the space station was created, the Foundation concludes that the crew members created it. There's a mystery over where the crew comes from, why they built the space station, etc., the Foundation decides this is worth investigating. Nothing here is unexpected, nor is it particularly engaging as payoff on a mystery. It's too predictable.

Additionally, there's a lack of detail on the latter half of your story. You describe the Foundation begins to investigate where the crew came from, why they built the ship, etc., but you don't actually answer any of these questions in your pitch nor do you describe the events of their investigation and (presumably) their discovery. This is the kind of detail we really need, as the latter half of a narrative can make or break it, and gaining an understanding of the full picture is important to making sure that the concept as a whole is viable.

By the end of the article, instead of knocking the scp out of orbit, the foundation decides to put the scp to use for research purposes.

This isn't a huge issue in and of itself, but it's indicative of other issues. On it's own, this isn't interesting enough. It's a payoff without a setup; why should the reader care whether the Foundation decides to use this space station for their own purposes? Unless it's been established that the reader should care about this, they probably won't, and therefore this ending will feel very flat and un-satisfying to most readers. As an ending it's not momentous or shocking enoughto justify itself without a strong setup, but it also lacks that setup, hence it just feels flat.

I'd really recommend putting some thought into what the emotion and ideas you want to convey to the reader here are. There's a distinct lack of this beyond "general mystery" and it means the concept as a whole lacks depth. Additionally, consider what you want the reader to latch onto here. What's the thing that's going to keep them reading? Why are they going to care about the story? Will it be the characters? The mystery? Something else? A finer focus in that regard would greatly benefit this concept.

item.title: Re: The rubbish station
item.content:encoded:
[Placeholder from PM - Expect crit within 24 hours]

my favorite kind of placeholder is the one that's only up for an hour

The Crit
Close

The SCP is a full functional space station, made out of wasted materials and it builds more modules if it collects more wasted materials.

So, a space station made of junk. Hm, it's fine? It's not particularly gripping to me, but it's not something I'd downvote based on. With a strong story, it could be good.

So, looking at your narrative, it's lacking in a progression. You've got a narrative premise, but not what happens next. It's lacking detail and a strong arc to keep the reader engaged. To address the narrative premise first:

A group of people wanted to create a breakaway civilisation, due to political difficulties, and considering they didn't have much, they wanted to see if a space station made out of garbage was possible

This isn't very interesting to me. "They wanted to" isn't a particularly relatable or engaging motivation, so the reader has no incentive to care about why their doing it, or to be engaged in the creation for another reason.

You have, however, given yourself a small hook to build more onto. "Due to political difficulties". What are these difficulties? What's interesting about them? What happens amongst these people? And most importantly, how is this going to be reflected in their creation?

Here's my recommendation - change it so this is instead a group of people who created a space station/ship of some sort in order to escape political discord. Something happened that meant they abandoned it, and it began to build itself anomalously. From here, you can build a narrative that explores what these political difficulties were, why it caused these people to leave, and how this is reflected in the creation itself.

What you have right now is lacking in the necessary detail, but if you were to use the hook that is present and build on that, I think you could build a compelling narrative.

I hope this feedback is helpful. Feel free to PM me again if you want me to take another look after you've developed the narrative here.

A group of people wanted to create a breakaway civilisation, duo to political difficulties, and considering they didn't have much,

If they remained poor and homeless (which is what I'm guessing your implying), how were they able to advance or have the supplies for space travel? breakaway civilisation, duo to political difficulties,

What does this add to the foundation and the law it carries, self-building trash? Like I've said before your idea doesn't add much to the story of the site, although, I do believe this does have heaps of potential behind it, and it could be turned into something truly great. Diary entries, discovery logs and a dark secret hidden just below a fake facade it's really your decision, once you've tidy up the plot holes and my question, and just dig a little deeper you could have a really good article

Good luck
Dr G
